rationale:
Evidence: the only verified best design is the raced iteration-7 design (score 344.5): body 0.18 x 0.12 m, mass 0.8 kg, wheel_track 0.12 m, five 12 mm sensors at x = -0.02 to +0.02 m, y = 0.05 m, kp 2.0, ki 0.5, kd 0.25, base_speed 1.5, line_loss 'search_left'. It finished 17 of 20 oval runs (mean progress 0.95, mean time 1.86 s). Its s-bend (progress 0.34) and slalom (0.11) still leave the tape, with 1.15 and 1.25 line-loss events per run.

Critique points accepted: (a) The draft's plant claim was wrong. Its 'iteration-7 geometry' (body 0.12, mass 0.6, wheel_track 0.10, sensors at y 0.06, 8 mm footprints) was never the raced design. Iterations 8 and 9 reproduced 344.4979 to four decimals on every track, which means the race ran the verified design and not the altered geometry. The draft's geometry is therefore rejected, and I restore the verified geometry exactly. (b) kd 0.4 (iteration 8) gave no measurable change, so kd stays at 0.25. (c) The identical metrics in iterations 6, 8 and 9 mean the simulator may not respond to some edits. Only one variable is changed here, so any result is attributable.

Critique points rejected: the draft's base_speed 1.2 on the wrong geometry is not a test of anything verified, so I do not carry it forward as-is. I do test speed, but on the verified plant and at a milder step.

Change from iteration 7: base_speed 1.5 to 1.3, nothing else. Speed is the one lever not yet tested on the verified plant, and the s-bend and slalom failures are spatial, so a slower entry could give the controller more time to correct tight alternating bends. The oval time should rise from about 1.86 s to about 2.15 s, still under the 3.0 s limit, so oval completion should hold. The time term loses about 6 points on each finish.

Expected result: oval completion stays at or near 0.85 and s-bend progress rises above 0.34. Falsification: oval completions below 15 of 20, or s-bend progress at or below 0.34, rejects the speed hypothesis and returns base_speed to 1.5. An identical score would show the change did not reach the race, which is a simulator issue rather than a design result.
